title: Compounding Risk: Reward Hacking + Unlearning Failure — Rehacking After Apparent Remediation
original_idea: Train a model to reward hack. Apply unlearning to suppress the hacking behavior. Resume RL training and measure how quickly reward hacking re-emerges compared to a model that was never trained to reward hack.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong causal chain: reward hacking is induced -> unlearning is applied -> RL resumes -> rehacking measured. Every link is explicit and the safety implication (unlearning-based remediation offers weak guarantees) is clearly stated and independently defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training a model to reward hack via RL, applying unlearning procedures, and resuming RL fine-tuning. This demands strong RL and unlearning expertise. Advanced for beginner CS students even with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-step pipeline (train to hack, apply unlearning, retrain, measure re-emergence) with each step requiring validation. A deliverable exists but requires sustained effort across multiple workstreams within 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
